# A cherry-pick runs the drivers but finishes on its own - no pre-merge-commit
# hook, and `--continue` runs no pre-commit either. So it commits a merged log
# with nothing resealed, which is why a merge entry drops the root hash claim.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp changed.txt $TMPDIR/changed.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt t
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec sesam add t --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secrets'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'

# Master moves the log too, so the cherry-pick has to merge it semantically.
exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt t
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'master: change t'

exec git cherry-pick topic
stderr 'the audit log was therefore semantically merged'

# git had nothing to identify itself with when the driver ran (a cherry-pick sets
# no ref and no env until it stops), so the advice stays deliberately generic.
stderr 'finish the git operation you started'

# The picked object arrived, the log verifies, and sesam asks for the seal it is
# owed instead of erroring out.
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
stderr 'a seal is pending'
exec sesam status
stdout 'out of sync'

# Sealing after a reveal completes it. (Reveal first: the object git installed is
# the authoritative one, our plaintext is the pre-pick version.)
exec sesam reveal
exec cat s
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'seal after cherry-pick'
exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
! stderr 'a seal is pending'

-- base.txt --
line one
BASE
line three
-- changed.txt --
line one
CHANGED
line three
